tool_version: 0.1.1 (the 10 MB binary vendored at tools/bartender/m3_bartender/, with xtb-6.4.1)
invocation: bartender -refit -owntraj solute_heavy.dcd -noplot -cpus 8 solute_heavy.gro bartender.inp, inside the environment bartender_config.sh sets

fitted_against.trajectory: prod/lig.xtc, 2001 frames of the solute at 10 ps
fitted_against.geometry: the same run's lig.gro, heavy atoms only, in the molecule's own atom order

mapping.beads: the nine physical beads; the two ring virtual sites are dropped, because BARTENDER has no notion of one and there are no atoms in it to fit
mapping.note: the `[ atoms ]` types here are the mapping's, so the bonded index can key each fitted term by bead type

what_it_is: bonded parameters fitted to this project's own atomistic ensemble, not to BARTENDER's semiempirical sampling: `-refit` with `-owntraj` fits the given trajectory
what_it_is_not: not a validated force field: one fit, one molecule, one reference run
not a source of ring constraints: BARTENDER keeps those in its own `[ constraints ]` section, and a ring's constraint lengths belong to the mapping that drew the ring
not a replacement for the published Martini 3 lipid terms: it is preferred for the pairs it covers, and the rest still comes from the published sets
not independent of the mapping: it fits the bead partition that exists, so a grouping defect is fitted as faithfully as a correct one

fit_quality.note: BARTENDER reports an rmsd for every fitted term in the unit of its ordinate, and the file's comments carry them. The worst two are the ring pairs 2-3 and 5-6 at 4.23 and 4.64, which it also kept as constraints rather than bonds.
